title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning
claim: Local path-level repair of a generator either stays unsafe or gets stuck; steering the latent first yields safe, goal-reaching outputs.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked baselines left, large ours right; verdict labels beneath
description: The left column has two stacked boxes. The top box, 'Vanilla', shows a robot, a red fire hazard zone and a goal flag. Several trajectories cross the hazard on the way to the flag, and a red X with 'Unsafe' sits below. The bottom box, 'SafeFlowMatcher', shows a trajectory deflected around the hazard that ends at a red circled X. A warning triangle with 'Safe but stuck' sits below it. The large right box, 'Full LBS (Ours)', has two parts. On the left is a pink latent-space ellipse with a green 'Safe set'. A red dot z0 is linked by an arrow to a green dot z+, which sits inside the safe set. A big gray arrow labeled 'Optimized Latent Z+' leads to a robot and hazard scene. There, a green curved path goes around the hazard to the flag, and yellow and blue arrows mark behavior-level selection and path-level repair, as the legend explains. A green check with 'Safe and goal-reaching' sits below. Red hazard boxes and the green ours path draw the eye first.
caption: Latent Barrier Steering separates behavior selection from path repair. A vanilla flow-matching planner may generate a goal-reaching but unsafe rollout under a new constraint. A path-space CBF corrector such as SafeFlowMatcher can enforce safety locally, but may produce a trajectory that is safe while no longer reaching the goal when the selected behavior mode is blocked. LBS first steers the behavior latent from $z_0$ to $z_+$ toward a safer rollout, then applies path-level CBF repair only for residual violations, yielding a trajectory that is both safe and goal-reaching.
abstract: We introduce Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical semantic-to-path framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning. Existing control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filters for diffusion and flow-matching planners act locally on generated samples, either during sampling or after prediction. Such repair is effective for small violations, but can struggle when a new constraint blocks the whole selected behavior mode rather than merely perturbing it locally. LBS decouples behavior selection from path certification through two coordinated interventions: it first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margin, then decodes the steered latent and applies a path-space CBF quadratic program (QP) only for residual violations. We show that latent steering increases the margin available to the path-space corrector, yielding finite-time recovery guarantees and reduced correction burden. Experiments across navigation and robot end-effector planning tasks show that LBS preserves safety while improving goal reaching and reducing correction burden compared with path-level safety filters.
